title: x402 Payment Schemes — Overview
quote: exact: fixed-price requests where the buyer authorizes the advertised amount. upto: single-request usage-based billing where the buyer authorizes a maximum and the seller charges actual usage. batch-settlement: high-volume or repeated micropayments where per-request authorizations are accumulated against a reusable channel.

title: x402 Documentation — Protocol Overview
quote: Server responds with 402 Payment Required + payment details header... Server verifies payload (locally or via facilitator)... Facilitator submits to blockchain... Server delivers resource with settlement confirmation.

title: x402 — exact scheme
quote: fixed-price x402 payments where the buyer authorizes exactly the advertised amount. EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization is the default when available, commonly deployed with USDC. Permit2 supports ERC-20 tokens lacking EIP-3009 support.

title: x402 — upto scheme
quote: usage-based x402 payments where the buyer authorizes a maximum and the seller charges actual usage. The EVM variant uses Permit2 because the settled amount is not known when the buyer signs.

title: x402 — batch-settlement scheme
quote: stateless unidirectional payment channels where a buyer deposits ERC-20 funds into escrow once, then signs cumulative vouchers for each request. The server's channel manager periodically batches many vouchers and claims them in one transaction.

title: x402 — Networks & Token Support
quote: Exact Payment Scheme: Available on EVM, Solana, TON, Stellar, Aptos, and Hedera. Batch Settlement: EVM only.

title: x402 — Facilitator
quote: /verify: The resource server POSTs the payment payload and payment details here. /settle: the facilitator submits the payment to the blockchain and waits for confirmation.

title: x402 upto scheme specification
quote: Each authorization MUST be settled at most once. At verification: amount represents the authorized maximum. At settlement: amount represents actual charge (<= authorized maximum).

title: x402 exact EVM scheme specification
quote: Permit2 path uses permitWitnessTransferFrom through a canonical x402ExactPermit2Proxy contract. The spender must be the proxy address (0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001), deployed consistently across chains using CREATE2.

title: coinbase/x402 GitHub repository
quote: TypeScript primary SDK: npm install @x402/core @x402/evm @x402/svm @x402/fetch. Python and Go packages available.

title: Cloudflare — Launching the x402 Foundation
quote: Cloudflare is partnering with Coinbase to establish the x402 Foundation, shipping x402 support across Agents SDK and MCP Servers, and proposing a Deferred Payment Scheme that decouples cryptographic verification from financial settlement.

title: Introducing x402 V2
quote: V2 evolves the protocol based on six months of real-world usage across 100M+ payments. Developers register chains and payment schemes as plugins. Deprecated X-* headers replaced by PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and PAYMENT-REQUIRED.

title: Introducing x402: a new standard for internet-native payments
quote: Coinbase is launching x402, a payment protocol that enables instant stablecoin payments directly over HTTP.

title: X402 Protocol: The HTTP-native Payment Standard for Autonomous AI Commerce
quote: 156,000-163,000 weekly transactions by October 2025 representing 492% growth. However... much of these stats are likely inflated by the wave of x402 tokens according to Bankless analysis. The PING memecoin alone generated approximately 150,000 of these transactions.

title: x402 Protocol Explained — Stablecoin Insider
quote: Key headers include PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, and PAYMENT-RESPONSE. V2 is now recommended, introducing improved identifiers and modularity.

title: Coinbase Developer Documentation — Welcome to x402
quote: x402 is a new open payment protocol developed by Coinbase that enables instant, automatic stablecoin payments directly over HTTP.
